docs.title: Welcome to PAAF
docs.text: PAAF (Personalized Agentic Assistant Framework) is a local-first, privacy-preserving framework where the user owns the mind.

docs.title: Core Philosophy
docs.text:
1. User Owns the Mind: System prompts, model profiles, and peer routing rules are defined transparently in paaf.yaml.
  2. Nothing Hidden: Every system prompt and handoff instruction can be byte-exact inspected via paaf prompt.
  3. In-Process & Modular Skills: Extend assistant capabilities cleanly via versioned skills and MCP server integrations.

docs.title: paaf_llm.agent.Agent
docs.text: Main turn loop runner for conversation turns and prompt compilation.

docs.text: Staging-based installation engine for remote or local skills.

docs.title: paaf_core.config.store
docs.text: Atomic configuration reader/writer with optimistic revision lock.

docs.title: Agent Mesh Architecture
docs.text: PAAF features an LLM-driven agent mesh allowing specialized model profiles to delegate conversations seamlessly.

docs.title: Handoff Mechanism
docs.text:
• Peer Graphs: Profiles declare allowed target peers using the peers field in paaf.yaml.
  • Handoff Tools: For each declared peer, PAAF exposes a transfer_to_<peer> tool dynamically to the active agent.
  • Hop Budgeting: Configurable hop_budget prevents infinite handoff loops between models.
  • Trace Auditing: Every handoff step is recorded into local SQLite trace logs without external data egress.

docs.title: PAAF Security Architecture: Non-Defensive Prompt Injection Governance
Overview
docs.text:
PAAF (Personalized Agentic Assistant Framework) implements a non-defensive prompt injection governance model (TOOL-07, PERS-05, D-18).

Unlike traditional LLM wrappers that inject hidden system instructions to filter, sanitize, or guard prompt text, PAAF enforces absolute prompt transparency ("nothing hidden from the user", PERS-05).

docs.title: Core Security Principles
docs.text:
1. Zero Hidden Defensive Instructions (PERS-05):
  2. System prompts contain ONLY base agent instructions, declared skills, and explicit peer/mesh explainers.
  3. PAAF never injects secret prompt defenses, hidden guardrails, or instruction overrides.

  4. Automated CI testing (tests/test_no_hidden_defense.py) continuously verifies the complete absence of defensive prompt phrases across all composed prompts.

  5. Permission Tiers as Sole Injection Defense (TOOL-05, TOOL-07):

  6. Tool execution authority is governed exclusively by Permission Tiers (observe, act, confirm).
  7. observe: Read-only queries (e.g. date_time_lookup, history_lookup).
  8. act: Safe active tools (e.g. custom @tool functions, standard MCP tools).

  9. confirm: Actionable or high-risk tools (e.g. system modifications, file writes, code execution).

  10. Spoken Confirmation Interlock (TOOL-06):

  11. Any tool assigned confirm tier MUST pause execution and ask the user for explicit spoken confirmation.
  12. Prompt format is strictly clean and concise: "Can I use tool <name>?" (D-06).

  13. Non-affirmative responses or timeouts default to DENIED (D-08).

  14. Auditing and Verification:

  15. Every permission request, grant, and denial is logged as a non-repudiable audit row in paaf-trace.
  16. paaf prompt prints exact bytes sent to the model without alteration.

docs.title: paaf.yaml Configuration Reference
docs.text: paaf.yaml is the single source of truth for model profiles, reload tiers, secret key references, and skill configurations.

docs.title: Schema Overview
docs.text:
active_profile: assistant
fallback_chain:
  - fast_local
profiles:
  assistant:
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.1
    temperature: 0.7
    peers:
      - coding_specialist
    capabilities: "General assistant for everyday tasks"

  coding_specialist:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
    api_key_ref: anthropic_key
    capabilities: "Expert software engineer"

skills:
  git_helper:
    enabled: true
    path: .paaf/skills/git_helper
    permissions:
      exec: confirm

docs.title: Reload Tiers
docs.text: Config changes apply according to explicit reload tiers: - HOT: Takes effect immediately with no restart (e.g. enabling/disabling skills, updating permissions). - WARM: Takes effect on the next turn (e.g. temperature, system prompt updates). - COLD: Re-initializes subsystem (e.g. changing model name). - RESTART: Requires full process restart (e.g. changing provider or endpoint).

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get up and running with PAAF in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Install the monolithic framework from PyPI:

pip install paaf

To enable heavy LLM engine adapters (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic), install the optional [engine] extra:

pip install "paaf[engine]"

docs.title: 2. Initialize Configuration
docs.text:
Create a paaf.yaml in your workspace:

active_profile: main_assistant
profiles:
  main_assistant:
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.1
    capabilities: "General assistance and reasoning"

docs.title: 3. Inspect Composed Prompt
docs.text:
Run the prompt inspector to verify the byte-exact system prompt:

paaf prompt --config paaf.yaml

docs.title: 4. Start Chat
docs.text:
Run interactive chat:

paaf chat --config paaf.yaml

docs.title: Scope Boundaries & Roadmap
docs.text: PAAF maintains strict transparency regarding feature availability.

docs.title: Current Delivered Scope (Phases 1 - 6)
docs.text:
• Monolithic Python package (paaf)
  • Multi-model profiles, fallback chains, and reload tiers
  • LLM-driven handoff agent mesh with observer guardrails
  • Unified Tool Registry (built-in, MCP, skills) with permission tiers
  • Skill packaging, autodiscovery loader, and staging installation

docs.title: Explicit Non-Existent Scope (Phase 13 Roadmap)
docs.text:
The following components do NOT exist yet and are scheduled for future development in Phase 13:

  • Voice & Audio Graph Subsystem: Real-time STT/TTS audio streaming does not exist yet.
  • Session Barge-in & Interruption: Asynchronous session interruption does not exist yet.
  • Appliance Background Service: Daemon mode / systemd service wrapper does not exist yet.
  • Desktop UI Application: Graphical desktop app wrapper does not exist yet.

docs.title: Skill Authoring & Security
docs.text:
Skills extend PAAF assistants with @tool functions and system prompt persona fragments.

SECURITY NOTICE: Skills run in-process with no sandbox; manifest permissions provide disclosure, not process isolation. For untrusted code, use MCP servers.

docs.title: Authoring a Skill
docs.text:
A skill directory requires a skill.yaml manifest:

name: my_custom_skill
version: 1.0.0
description: Custom tools for task automation
tools:
  - my_tool
permissions:
  file_access: confirm

And python modules with @tool decorated functions:

from paaf_llm.tools.decorator import tool

@tool(description="Execute custom operation")
def my_tool(param: str) -> str:
    return f"Processed {param}"

docs.title: Installing Skills
docs.text:
Install via git URL or local path:

paaf skill install https://github.com/example/my_skill.git
